note: The sandbox base. pos is [x, z] in metres from the patch centre (+X east, -Z north), yaw degrees clockwise from north. Heights come from the terrain. Layout from real surface-base practice where we have it: power away from the habitat, the lander pad far off, Curiosity is a landmark toward Mount Sharp (it is really far up the mountain).

cables._note: power cables laid on the ground (world.gd _cables): polylines of [x, z], draped on height_at() every step m, width and height in metres, in a DESIGN.md role; rocks keep off them as off paths. The reactor's 3 kVac line comes in from 1 km in the real plan (NTRS 20250000841); our patch ends at 200 m, so the reactor stands near its west edge, 190 m out, and the line runs to HAB 1's utility panel. The field's header runs along the wings' north ends past each row's junction box (z 8.57), then to the batteries; theirs runs to the habitat. Size and route are ours

bound._note: where anything that moves may go: |x| and |z| up to half (m from the patch centre). The ground is real only on the 400 m patch (data/terrain.json, half 200): past it the backdrop is drawn with no collision, and height_at() reads the patch edge. 190 keeps a body's reach inside it: the rover's centre stays reach (m, its rear hatch) further in, and the cameras behind (5 m on foot, 9 m driving) stay over the patch. Near the line the hero and the rover slow at their own braking (reality.json hero.stop, rover.brake) and stop on it. The safety net (sandbox.gd): a body found more than below (m) under the ground, or past the line, goes back on top at the nearest spot inside, behind a short fade (fade_s) when that is further than fade_over (m). Art direction

kinds._note: how an item collides; anything not named here is a static (layer 2, or 3 when narrower than the hero)

sink._note: how far each prefab sits in the dust: a reality.json row id per prefab, else default (skills/shadows-and-grounding, Sink). support: metres above an item's lowest drawn point that still count as resting on the ground (feet, skids, bevelled bottom edges). level: prefabs crews build level (floors, foundations, tracking mounts); everything else tilts to the ground under it, as a lander's legs or a bag do. Vehicles only touch: their drivers set them on their wheels, sunk by their own row here (rover). Rocks: reality.json rock.embed

_swept_range_m: metres from the camera to a ground cell's centre (the patch centre for the base) beyond which its swept surfaces (floors, HAB 1's fit-out: DESIGN.md weathering.clean) are not drawn: seen only through doorways, they cost a draw call each from anywhere (world.gd _merge). Art direction
_lit_roles: roles a sky state lights pane by pane (DESIGN.<state>.md `lit`, house_style): their panes are numbered when the meshes merge at load, whichever sky is up then

blink._note: status lights that flash on their own (world/machines.gd): nodes named by `nodes` keep their own mesh and a copy of the light role. hz and duty: an obstruction beacon flashes 20 to 40 times a minute (FAA L-864 red 20 to 40, L-865 white 40, https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/150-5345-43GH.pdf, from a search summary); WCAG 2.3.1 allows at most 3 flashes in any second. off: the share of the light left when it is dark

machines._note: the base working on its own (world/machines.gd). tracker: solar panels start facing the sun and turn to it about their tube at slew_deg_s (after a sky switch or a tilt by hand) within limit_deg (30 keeps a panel's low edge at the 0.82 m of its 30 degree rest, above a walker's knees), re-aiming when the sun is step_deg off, lying flat (stow) where weather says stow (night, storm), and holding still for pause_s after anyone else moves one (the tilt interaction). dish: nods nod_deg either side of its rest every period_s at slew_deg_s. near_m: panels and dish hold still while the hero is this close (a machine stops when people come near). All art direction; servo: the sound each move starts with, played only within hear_m (Mars sound 'falters at just 26 feet (8 meters)', NASA/JPL 2022)

tracker._rows: per prefab: gcr, the ground coverage ratio of its rows (panel chord over row pitch), with which the rows backtrack toward flat when the sun is low enough for a row to shade the next (Anderson and Mikofski 2020, NREL/TP-5K00-76626; pvlib tracking.singleaxis, whose example is 2 m modules 6 m apart, gcr 1/3; design/research/pages/tracker/). solar_array: 2.5 m panels in two rows 8 m apart. solar_wing: 2.5 m wings 7.5 m apart, the six rows running north and south as single-axis trackers usually do (Sandia PVPMC), turning to limit_deg 45, 'common' for trackers (Sandia PVPMC); its low edge then stands 0.57 m up, and the field has no walkway under it

telltale._note: Phoenix's Telltale (2008): a light Kapton tube on Kevlar fibres from a gallows on the met mast, its tilt read off camera images. tilt: [wind m/s, tilt rad] at 8 mbar, read off Fig. 25 of the Telltale calibration report (Gunnlaugsson et al., https://pds.nasa.gov/data/pds4/1000/tt_bundle_1000/document/TELLTALECALRPT.PDF; design/research/pages/alive/telltale.md): thin air barely moves it, about 1 degree at 4 m/s. flutter: the share of the tilt it trembles by (the report reads turbulence from the image blur), flutter_hz how fast; art direction

grounding._note: the ground's answer under everything that rests on it (world.rest(), terrain.gdshader): a soft darkening where the sky is blocked (AO scales the ambient light only, skills/shadows-and-grounding section 4) plus a little in the albedo, and a faint rim of dust pushed up around the edge (a normal tilt). radius: m a foot's shadow reaches past it; ao, albedo: how much at the foot; pile: the rim's strength; px: the map's pixels over play_half; set_down_speed (m/s) and set_down_strength: the grit a bag throws when it is put down (world.puff). Art direction

paths._note: walkways kept clear of rocks: polylines of [x, z], width in metres

scatter._note: rocks over the patch: none on items, pads or paths, densest just outside the base clearing. Sizes in metres; rocks in big_size are solid, pebbles are not

wind._note: toward_deg: where the wind blows to, degrees clockwise from north (a design choice: no measured Gale direction found). Speeds per sky state in weather: Ingenuity's dust drifted downwind at 4 to 6 m/s (research/godot-build/movement-and-look.md section 4)
wind._gust: gust(): one slow swell every wind listener reads (dust streaks, the wind sound, the telltale; skills/living-atmosphere section 2). gust_hz: the noise's frequency, so a swell takes tens of seconds; share: how far a gust takes the sky state's speed above or below it. Both art direction: no measured Gale gust timing in our sources

weather._note: dust effects per sky state, keyed by the DESIGN.<state>.md name. streaks: share of the wind streaks shown; devil: the far dust devil (summer afternoons, NASA 2017); front: the storm's close dust clouds; stow: the solar trackers lie flat (no sun at night; trackers stow flat in high wind)

contact._note: footstep and wheel dust (skills/ground-contact-fx, design/research/dust.md). Grit: grains over ~70 um launched at 30 to 60 deg (Kok 2012), each gone when it lands, T = 2 v sin(theta) / g with g from reality.json; a wheel throws them backward and low (fenders, NASM 2015). Haze: dust under ~20 um in the bottom few cm, spreading then drifting downwind and gone in 2 to 3 s (Lemmon 2022). min_speed (nothing thrown standing still), counts, sizes (grit_size: a few pixels at the 4.2 m play camera, ground-contact-fx section 3), alpha and the speed spread are art direction. foot_kick: the share of the walking speed a boot's push-off scuffs grit backward at (the boot is nearly still at contact; ground-contact-fx section 2), art direction. wheel_grit, wheel_grit_size, wheel_haze: a rolling wheel's steady stream (dust.stream()): grains alive at once, their size (a few pixels at the 9 m driving camera, ground-contact-fx section 3) haze quads alive at once, their peak alpha and size (a 3 t rover lifts more fine dust than a boot, and grit the ground's colour vanishes against the ground); art direction

devil._note: the dust devil wanders round the base centre this far out, in and out by the share `wander`, at this speed in m/s; day only (weather), the summer afternoons NASA saw them at Gale (sol 1597). All design choices (no measured Gale speed in our sources): slow enough to watch, outside the lander and Curiosity, near enough to see from the base (at 160 m it did not show)

probe._note: one reflection probe over the base: centre [x, z], size [x, y, z]. The sandbox redraws every probe from this centre looking north after a sky switch (HouseStyle.warm()), and a probe is drawn only once a camera sees it: the centre sits 10 m south of HAB 1 so the room probes are in view. rooms: an item's own probe, centre `at` and `size` in its space (HAB 1: the room between the deck at 0.40 m and the ceiling at 2.72 m)

pip._note: PIP's wandering (sandbox/pip.gd): ambient life, no game state. Speed, acceleration and turn: reality.json pip.*. Everything here is art direction. stops: where it parks [x, z] and what it looks at [x, z, height above the ground], weight how often it picks one; via: open ground it may drive through, so the route graph (every straight, clear line between stops and via points, `clearance` m clear either side) gets round the buildings; via_m: how near a via point counts as passed;  (the lander is a long trip), divided by near_m plus the distance so near stops come up more; never one of the last two. notice_m: the hero this close gets a look, a beep and two flashes (flash_hz under the 3 a second limit), at most every hello_cool_s. A hero standing still (below still_speed m/s for still_s) within greet_m gets a visit: PIP parks greet_stand_m away, looks up with its head tilted, wiggles, for greet_s, then not again for greet_cool_s. yield_m, yield_deg: a hero this close inside this cone ahead stops it for wait_s, then it drives round for patience_s. feeler_m: how far ahead it checks, every feel_s; stuck_s without getting 0.3 m closer and it goes elsewhere. door_clear_m round every door and rooms (prefabs, grown by room_margin) it never drives into. flee_m: a moving rover this close sends it aside. Head: yaw and pitch limits, turn rate, tilt; blinks every blink_s, double_blink share; status bar glows at glow_hz. track_every, track_width: m between wheel prints (a print is 0.12 m long, world/terrain.gd, so under that they join into a band) and their width (the wheel is 8 cm wide, forge/vehicle_pip.py); shade: contact shadow radius and strength

views._note: eye-height capture views at 1.6 m over the floor (lane B, interiors): [from, at], heights over the ground like sandbox.gd VIEWS

rooms._note: the buildings whose inside puts the view in first person (player.gd _room, skills/third-person-camera Into first person indoors): each item id's floor plan in its own space, circles [x, z, r] and rects [x0, z0, x1, z1], measured from the models (12 Nov). hab1: building_habitat.glb floor x and z +-2.40, the door's inner face at z -2.16. greenhouse: building_greenhouse.glb floor +-3.28 (the dome), and the vestibule x +-1.0 from the door's inner face at z -4.46 to the dome. The doorway band is the hero's own radius either side of these lines

plants._note: lettuce in the greenhouse grow-bed slots (slot_N nodes of its model), one growth stage per slot; stage 4 is a harvest-size head (reality.json lettuce.width). A prefab id instead of a stage goes in at its own size: HAB 1's Veggie unit on the galley counter
